rv.q: This West End transfer is a success – the Ambassadors' petite stage perfectly conjures a black and white television screen blown up to theatrical proportions.
...even if the show doesn’t always hang together as a whole, it’s still enjoyable and entertaining.
Yet for all that skill, The Twilight Zone play comes to feel like a bad idea, well executed.
Spooky TV tribute could do with an extra dimension.
The result is a show that feels oddly cheaper than the original – and weirdly unexciting.
Anne Washburn's play for the Almeida achieves lift-off in the West End...Definitely worth the rocket ride.
I don't think fans of the TV series will come away from this moody, classy stage distillation feeling short-changed...A shudder-inducingly good night out.

cn.t: Anne Washburn's stage adaptation receives mixed reviews, with critics praising its theatrical inventiveness but noting the tales have lost their terror and now play more for laughs than scares.
